prompt: Why can't training error be used to judge a model?
options: It is systematically optimistic: the model was fitted to those exact points
explanation: The weights were chosen to make that error small, so it underestimates the error on new data, more so for flexible models.

prompt: Training error 0.001, validation error 0.4. This indicates...
options: a bug in the loss only
explanation: A huge gap between training and validation error is the signature of overfitting. Remedies: more data, regularisation, a simpler model.

prompt: Training error 0.4, validation error 0.42. This indicates...
options: underfitting (high bias): the model is too simple
explanation: Both errors are high and close: the model cannot even fit the training data. Use a richer model or better features; more data will not help.

prompt: The expected squared error at a point decomposes as...
In 5-fold cross-validation, how many times is each example used for validation?
explanation: Each point is in exactly one fold, so it is used for validation once and for training in the other four rounds.

prompt: You standardise the whole data set, then split into folds. What is wrong?
options: Validation folds influenced the mean/std used on the training folds: data leakage
explanation: Any statistic computed with validation points leaks information. Fit the scaler on the training folds only, inside each fold.
Stronger shrinkage makes the model more rigid: it deviates more from the truth on average (bias) but is less sensitive to the training sample (variance).

prompt: For hourly sensor data you want to forecast tomorrow. Which split is appropriate?
options: Train on the past, validate on a later period
Train on the future, validate on the past
Any split gives the same result
explanation: A random shuffle lets the model peek at neighbours of the validation points in time. Respect the order in which the model will be used.
